paragraphs: Jesus does not do lukewarm, friend, and I've had lukewarm ovens, so I know nothing good comes out of those. He says, "I have come to ignite a fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!" (Luke 12:49). Then He says peace isn't what He brings: "No, I tell you, but division" (Luke 12:51). I think the lesson is that following Jesus is never a background setting. Even a household can end up split over Him (Luke 12:52-53).

Then Jesus points to something the crowds do well. They see a cloud and call the rain, and they feel the south wind and call the heat (Luke 12:54-55). So He asks why they don't know how to interpret "the present time" (Luke 12:56). You'd check the forecast three times before a road trip, but ignore the most important thing happening right in front of you? He also asks why they don't "judge for yourselves what is right" (Luke 12:57). I think that means Jesus wants us paying attention, not coasting.

Next Jesus gives them a road with a magistrate at the end of it. He says to "make every effort to reconcile with your adversary" while you're still on the way (Luke 12:58). Wait too long and it ends with the prison and the "very last penny" (Luke 12:59). It's like that group chat you keep not answering, friend, because the longer you wait, the bigger it gets. So the big idea is to wake up to what Jesus is doing now, and to deal with what's in front of you while there's still road left.
